parties:
Saitan Bibi and others ------Plaintiff-Appellant
vs
Chairan Bewa and others ------ Defendant-Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff filed the suit for permanent injunction restraining defendant No.1 from disturbing the plaintiffs' peaceful possession in the suit land. The plaint case is that the suit jote appertaining to CS Khatian No.377 of Rasulpur Mouja belong to defendant Nos.1-2 as chaua rayat at a rental of 9 maunds 18 seers and 12 chataks paddy under Sharat Shundari Devi. Defendants Asiruddin Mondal and Easin Ali Mondal possessed the suit jote in equal share and the CS khgtian was prepared in their names accordingly. During the revisional rent roll operation the suit jote was also recorded in the names of the defendants and the paddy rent has been commuted into money rent of Rs.3/55 and they paid rents of the jote to the Government. Defendant No. 1 transferred more than 10 bighas of land in violation of Ordinance No. XXXIII of 1951 For this offence defendant No. 1 was fined as he did not pay the fine in time. A Certificate Case No. 6 AM/59-60 was started in the Bogra Certificate Court and after due service of the processes and observance of the relevant provisions of law the suit land and other lands of defendant No. 1 was auction sold to the plaintiffs on 10-8-62 after due publicity and within the knowledge of defendant No. 1. The sale was confirmed on 15-10- 62. The plaintiff got the sale certificate and took the delivery of possession of the auction purchased land on 8-12-62 by beat of drum and since then they have been possessing the land by personal cultivation, After taking delivery of possession the plaintiff by amicable partition with proforma defendant No. 2 got the suit land and have been in exclusive possession of the same. Defendant No. 1 no interest and possession in the suit land. But defendant No. 1 has recently created some dakhilas in the name of his wife and in collusion with the settlement employee caused the MR Khatian of the suit land to be prepared in the name of his wife. The story of pattan of the suit land in the name of his wife is fictitious and the plaintiff got the MR Khatian corrected in their names on application under section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act to the Revenue Officer on 24-12-66. At this defendant No.1 became very enraged and on 8- 3-67 defendant No.1 came to the suit land to resist the plaintiff and his laborers to plough the land and the plaintiff drove away defendant No. 1. But while leaving the spot he threatened that he will possess the suit land by any means. These activities on the part of defendant No. 1 have caused breach of peace and irreparable loss to the plaintiff. Hence the suit. 

 3. Defendant No. 1 appeared and contested the suit by filing written statement wherein he denied all the allegations made in the plaint. The defence case, in short, is as follows: The suit is not maintainable in this form and that the suit is barred by limitation and adverse possession. He further contended that for high rate of paddy rent defendant No.1 surrendered 0.58 decimals of land of the suit khatian in favour of the ex-landlord from whom Pasiran, wife of this defendant, took pattan of the said land on 13-11-1355 BS at a rental of Rs. 1 annas 12 and paisa 6. Since the time of pattan she possessed the suit land exclusively. During the revisional settlement the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of defendant No.1 and on filing objection Pasiran Bibi got the khatian corrected in her name and she paid rent to the Government. The auction purchase was held behind the knowledge of this defendant. But the wife of this defendant, Pasiran Bibi was in possession of the suit land since long before the certificate case. Defendant No.1 had no interest in the suit land at the time of auction sale. If there is any auction sale of the suit land, it is fraudulent and void and by such sale the interest of Pasiran has not been affected and the plaintiff never got possession of the suit land by virtue of such void sale. While in possession Pasiran Bibi transferred the suit land to her two daughters, Saleha and Hamida by registered kabala deed dated 22-9-66, on receipt of consideration. Thereafter, Pasiran Bibi died on 14-11-66. After the kabala purchase, Saleha and Hamida have been possessing the suit land. The plaintiffs in collusion with Altaf Ali Miah their brother-in-law and the Tahsilder of Khetlal Tahsil Office fraudulently got the suit land recorded in their names under section 143 of the said Act behind the knowledge of the kabala purchasers. This record is collusive and has not conferred any title and interest on the plaintiff in respect of the suit land. The plaintiffs have no interest and possession in the suit land. Defendant No. 1 never resisted the plaintiffs on 23rd Falgoon, 1373 BS or on any other date. The story of the cause of auction is fictitious. The suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. The learned Assistant Judge on consideration of the oral and documentary evidences on record disbelieved the auction sale and believed the dakhilas Exts. A-A(3) which show that Pasiran Bibi paid rents of the land to ex-landlord from 1355 BS to 1358 BS. The trial Judge also believed Exts. A(4) to A(6), dakhilas which also show that Pasiran Bibi paid rents to the Government for the years from 1359 BS to 1372 BS. The trial Judge also believed the certified copy of MR Khatian No. 421, Ext. B recorded in the name of Pasiran Bibi in respect of the suit land. Ext. C the certified copy of the order of the Revenue Circle Officer in a proceeding under section 19(1) of the State Acquisition Act,1950 shows that the MR Khatian was prepared in the name of Pasiran Bibi. On consideration of the documentary evidences on record the learned Assistant Judge held that Pasiran Bibi acquired right, title, interest and possession in the suit land by virtue of the pattan before the certificate case was started. Consequently held that the interest of Pasiran was not affected by the auction sale held in pursuance of the certificate proceeding against defendant No. 1 as Pasiran Bibi was not a party to the certificate proceeding and she said sale is not binding upon Pasiran Bibi, wife of defendant No. 1. The learned Assistant Judge also believed Ext. D the registered kabala whereby Pasiran transferred her interest in the suit land in favour of her two daughters, Saleha Bibi and Hamida Bibi. Upon consideration of the entire materials on record the Assistant Judge found that the plaintiffs failed to prove prima facie title in the suit land and dismissed the suit. 

 5. The learned Subordinate Judge as the last court of fact reversed the judgment of the trial Court and believed the auction purchase of the plaintiff in a certificate proceeding and found title and possession in favour of the plaintiff. The learned Subordinate Judge disbelieved the story of surrender of the suit land as the paddy rent of the holding was excessive and thereafter fresh lease in respect of the suit land at a money rent was taken by the plaintiff from the landlord before the alleged auction sale. The learned Subordinate Judge disbelieved the alleged surrender as it appeared to him that the evidence is weak and discrepant. The learned Subordinate Judge found that defendant No. 1 had subsisting interest when the alleged certificate proceeding started. The lower appellate Court disbelieved the story of surrender as the surrender was partial without the consent of the co- sharer brother, defendant No. 2. The learned Subordinate Judge further found that the certificate proceeding was conducted as per Rules and plaintiff auction purchased on 10-8-62 and went into possession. The lower appellate Court disbelieved the defendants story of surrender in favour of the landlord and subsequent pattan in the name of his wife Pasiran Bibi and decreed the suit. 

 7. Leave was granted to consider whether the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division was correct in interfering with the finding of fact of the last court of fact in his revisional jurisdiction when the lower appellate Court after due consideration of the oral and documentary evidences on record arrived at a finding of fact. Leave was also granted to consider whether the finding of the learned Single Judge that there was no cause of action for filing of the suit as the threatened dispossession by defendant No. 1 does not exist after his death and there was no fresh threat from the heirs of defendant No. 1 and whether the learned Single Judge was correct in holding that the suit will fail for defect of parties as the subsequent alleged kabala purchasers namely, the two daughters of defendant No. 1 as well as wife Pasiran Bibi in whose favour fresh pattan was given were not made parties in the suit. 

 8. The learned Single Judge found that in the written statement defendant No. 1 clearly stated that he took pattan of 0.58 acres of suit land from Ex. Rent Receiver in the name of his wife as back as in 1355 BS by Exts. A-2. The learned Single Judge believed the rent receipts of Pasiran and paying of rents to the Ex Rent Receiver and thereafter to the Government. The learned Single Judge considered the exhibits namely, the dakhilas and the MR Khatian and found clear prima facie title of Pasiran Bibi. The learned Single Judge also found that Pasiran transferred her 0.58 acres of land to her two daughters by registered Kabala. The learned Single Judge found that the last court of fact has not given due consideration to the oral and documentary evidences on record as has been produced by the defendant and wrongly reversed the findings of the trial Court. The learned Single Judge also found that the lower appellate Court unreasonably placed more reliance on the material oral evidence of the plaintiff's witnesses and disbelieved the deposition of defendants' witness without giving any valid and cogent reasons. The learned Single Judge also found that the finding of the lower appellate Court with regard to question of partial surrender is also not legally tenable. The learned Single Judge found that the lower appellate Court wrongly found that defendant No. 1 alone surrendered the suit land without the consent of his co-sharer brother defendant No. 2. It is on record that by amicable arrangements defendant Nos. 1 and 2 were possessing separately and, as such, defendant No.2 was not a party to the alleged surrender and consent of defendant No.2 as co-sharer was not at all necessary as per section 86(7) of Bengal Tenancy Act. This material aspect was lost sight of by the lower appellate Court which wrongly found fault with defendant No. 2 for not appearing to depose in the case. Thus, the reasons given by the lower appellate Court for non-appearance of defendant No. 2 was wrong as found by the learned Single Judge. In such circumstances, the learned Single Judge on due consideration of the oral and documentary evidences on record found that the finding of fact arrived at by the lower appellate Court is based on misreading and non-consideration of the material evidence on record and consequently interfered with the findings of fact arrived at by the lower appellate Court.
